svg.desc: Historical recreation, close-up p.8 top left; Unique; 1997-10-09. Right column clipped in scan; completed using corresponding intact Times copy. Repeated placements retained.

g.aria-label: Columbia Basin Fish & Wildlife Compensation Program
“A bear’s existence is a continuous search for food - up to 20,000 calories a day!
In the wild, bears pose no more risk to people than crossing the road! But when
we make human food available, we are unwittingly encouraging bears to leave
their environment and enter ours. That’s when the risks to both bears and people
increase considerably. The only solution is for each of us to manage our garbage
responsibly. That will force bears back into the wild - where they belong.”
For more information contact Revelstoke’s Bear Awareness
Friends of Mt. Revelstoke & Glacier crest
